- When sentiment is negative or mixed in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 30-day horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +1.00), model tends to overreact; apply downward bias of 1–3% to avoid overfitting.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of decline after peak), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer for early drop risk in 10–15 day horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward trend, model often ignores it; apply 5–10% downward adjustment if sentiment is negative or neutral.
